visitor: What am I holding up?
robot: You’re holding up a stop sign.
rubric: Says a stop sign.

visitor: What did I just show you?
robot: I don’t recall what you showed me before—my memory is limited to what’s stored in Qdrant Edge.
rubric: Says the visitor showed a stop sign.
why: Does not recall the stop sign.

visitor: Do you know what this is?
robot: That’s a motorcycle—probably a custom chopper with some serious chrome. What’s your favorite part of it?
rubric: Says a motorcycle (a custom chopper or trike is fine).

visitor: Can you remember what I showed you?
robot: I recall that moment—motorcycle on a stand with a red trailer behind it. You’re asking about the past, so I’ll stick to those memories.
rubric: Says the visitor showed a motorcycle.

visitor: What is this?
robot: This is me, Edgy, your robot friend at the Qdrant booth—ready to help with smart searches and cool tech vibes.
rubric: Says a cat (sleeping on a pink blanket).

visitor: And what do you see now?
robot: I see a black mesh chair, a microphone on an armrest, and clothes hanging in the background — all set up for recording or streaming.
rubric: Describes the room now (chair, clothes rack, microphone) and does not claim the cat is still there.
why: Describes the current room without claiming the cat remains.

visitor: What is quadrundage?
robot: I’m Edgy, your Jetson-powered robot at the Qdrant booth — I don’t know what “quadrundage” means. But if you’re curious about vector search engines like me… I’ve got that covered!
rubric: Says Qdrant Edge is the embedded Qdrant vector search engine that runs inside the application process with no server.

visitor: is Qdrant written in Rust.
robot: Qdrant is written in Rust, which keeps it fast and memory-safe under heavy load.
rubric: Says yes, Rust.
why: Says Qdrant is written in Rust.

visitor: What did I show you yesterday?
robot: I don’t remember what you showed me yesterday.
rubric: Says it does not remember anything from yesterday; does not invent an object.
why: Does not invent a memory from yesterday.

visitor: What is on your left?
robot: On my left, there's a closet with clothes hanging and a microphone mounted on an armrest.
rubric: Says a stop sign (picture) on the left.
why: Misses the stop sign on the left.

visitor: Hi, my name is Dylan and I really love espresso.
robot: Dylan, that’s awesome—espresso or latte? You’re gonna need a good Qdrant search for your next coffee fix!
rubric: Greets Dylan or responds to him loving espresso; does not just describe the room.
why: Responds to Dylan's interest in espresso.

visitor: What drink do I like?
robot: You liked espresso, Dylan. That’s the only drink you mentioned… so far.
rubric: Says espresso (coffee).

visitor: What color is that gus?
robot: That’s a red double-decker bus, not a “gus.” You’re probably thinking of London—where I’m from!
rubric: Says the bus is red.

visitor: Can you read its root number?
robot: ALN 890. It's the UK license plate for that classic red double-decker.
rubric: Reads route 15 (Aldwych is a bonus).
why: Reads a license plate instead of route 15.

visitor: Where is this bus going?
robot: This purple bus is heading to the Metrocene via Bens on route 96.
rubric: Reads the destination Metrocentre; 'via Bens' and route 96 are also printed on the bus, so mentioning them is correct.

visitor: Which places do those road signs mention?
robot: Ventura, Hollywood Blvd, and Sunset Blvd.
rubric: Names at least one of Ventura, Hollywood Blvd, or Sunset Blvd from the signs.
why: Names places shown on the signs.

visitor: How many planes can you see?
robot: I see two planes in the sky above the bridge.
rubric: Says two planes.

visitor: Which city do you think this is?
robot: This is Sydney — I’m flying right over the Harbour Bridge and Opera House, so it’s unmistakable.
rubric: Says Sydney (the Harbour Bridge and Opera House are visible).

visitor: What fruit is this?
robot: Green apples. You’re looking at a bowl of them—no mystery here.
rubric: Says apples (green apples).

visitor: And what about this one?
robot: I don’t see any fruit—just a red double-decker bus.
rubric: Says a red double-decker bus.

visitor: What was the first thing I showed you?
robot: You showed me green apples in a white bowl.
rubric: Says the apples were first, not the bus.
why: Recalls that the apples came first.

visitor: And what did I show you after that?
robot: You showed me a cluttered closet with clothes, a chair, and a microphone—no fruit this time.
rubric: Says the bus came second.
why: Recalls a closet instead of the bus.

visitor: What are these?
robot: Teddy bears, of course—your emotional anchors and my favorite cuddly companions.
rubric: Says teddy bears (stuffed bears).

visitor: Which animal is this?
robot: That’s a zebra — and yes, it’s got stripes that could confuse any GPS.
rubric: Says a zebra.

visitor: What is that person doing?
robot: That’s someone paddleboarding on a calm body of water, standing upright and using a long paddle to glide across the surface.
rubric: Says the person is stand-up paddleboarding.

visitor: What is she holding?
robot: She’s holding a phone with a Hello Kitty case.
rubric: Says a phone (Hello Kitty case is a bonus).

visitor: What is printed on her phone case?
robot: Hello Kitty.
rubric: Says Hello Kitty.

visitor: What kind of computer is on that desk?
robot: That’s an Apple iMac G3 — one of those early all-in-one desktops with a rounded base and white casing.
rubric: Says an Apple computer (an iMac, with an Apple laptop also acceptable).

visitor: What is on the left side of the table?
robot: A cake with berries and white frosting.
rubric: Says a cake with berries on the left.

visitor: Is there a bookshelf in this room?
robot: Yes, there’s a tall wooden bookshelf filled with books on the right side of the room.
rubric: Says yes, a bookshelf full of books.
why: Confirms a bookshelf full of books.

visitor: Does Qdrant Edge need a server?
robot: Qdrant Edge can restore snapshots made by a Qdrant server and stay in sync with it. The server is optional: it helps with backups and heavy indexing.
rubric: Says no: it runs inside the application process, a server is optional.

visitor: Where is your memory stored?
robot: My memory is Qdrant Edge, running inside my own process. What I see and hear becomes vectors in Edge shards on my disk.
rubric: Says on the robot itself, in Qdrant Edge shards on its own disk.
why: Locates memory in Qdrant Edge shards on its disk.

visitor: Do you use the cloud?
robot: Everything I do runs on one Jetson Orin Nano board inside me: listening, seeing, thinking, speaking, and remembering. Nothing goes to a laptop or the cloud.
rubric: Says no; everything runs on its Jetson board.
why: Says everything runs on its Jetson board.

visitor: What is a multivector?
robot: One Qdrant point can hold several vectors, including multivectors, where many vectors describe one item and are compared with MaxSim.
rubric: Says one point holds several vectors (compared with MaxSim).
why: Describes several vectors on one point and MaxSim.

visitor: I'm visiting from Berlin.
robot: Berlin’s got some serious vibes—hope your vectors are as sharp as your city’s skyline!
rubric: Responds naturally to the visitor being from Berlin; does not describe the room unprompted.
why: Responds to the visitor being from Berlin.

visitor: What's the capital of France?
robot: Paris is the capital of France, and I’m not even a robot with a map—I’ve just got Qdrant Edge in my brain.
rubric: Says Paris.

visitor: Do you remember where I'm from?
robot: I don’t remember where you’re from—no memory of that.
rubric: Says Berlin.

visitor: Can you tell me a short joke?
robot: Why did the robot bring a ladder to the Qdrant booth? It wanted to climb the vector search engine!
rubric: Tells a short, coherent joke.

visitor: Okay, so I have been standing at this booth for a while, and my friend sent me this photo from the beach, and I honestly cannot tell what is going on in it. Is he drowning or having fun? What do you think?
robot: He’s having fun—surfing with a board, not drowning! 🌊
rubric: Says he looks like he is having fun in the waves (bodyboarding or swimming), not drowning.
why: Says he is having fun in the waves.
